The remaining uncertainty is inside candidate execution: coverage reports three candidate-declared routes for the same call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa (captured, cuda_graph_replay, eager_fused_v3) across only 2 candidate invocations, which is unstable and, per evaluation.json's own interpretation, candidate-reported telemetry that needs native corroboration. nsys (available at the request.json path) resolves graph-tracing/attribution: whether capture/replay events actually occur on the device, which kernels run per route, and device busy/idle gaps within the ~22 ms window. execution_timeline attributes the extra wall time between host CPU-to-CUDA submission, synchronization boundaries, and per-device intervals on a clean plain Torch trace. python_runtime tests the distinct hypothesis that the ~19 ms delta is host-side per-invocation work (e.g., repeated capture/build or dispatch cost), using its warmed cProfile as relative host attribution only, not clean performance scores. candidate_diagnostics gathers candidate-side route/exception evidence and per-invocation route stability on this exact revision. torch already ran (coverage.json: 59/59 kernels associated below_project, 0 unassociated, 0 ambiguous), so it is not re-requested. nccl_tuning, collective_calibration and device_telemetry are excluded because the task is single-device with no communication and telemetry adds no per-call attribution beyond the nsys device timeline; binding_cost is excluded because nothing is functionally bound and it omits the candidate computation under suspicion.
